messages.content:
Two readers answered the same question about machines at work. Reader A used facts taken from a fact
store; each fact comes with the sentence it was taken from. Reader B read the documents directly and points at
sentences. Decide which answer the evidence supports. Use only the evidence shown; do not use what you know.

Rules:
- An answer is supported only if its evidence states it for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the
  same article and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline, the same condition the question
  states). Evidence about a neighbouring subject does not support an answer.
- When the two rest on texts of different rank, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's
  manual, then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.)
  wins over a ministerial decree (DM). A wording corrected by a corrigendum replaces the original wording.
- For a list, prefer the answer whose items are each stated by the evidence and that leaves none out.
- If reader B found nothing, decide only whether A's evidence really states A's answer for the exact subject.
- "same" means the two answers say the same thing. "neither" means neither answer is supported.
Return JSON only: {"reasoning": "two or three short sentences", "choice": "A" | "B" | "same" | "neither"}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: Which essential requirement on protection against corruption does the Regulation introduce that the Directive did not have?

Answer A: ["software and data critical for compliance with the relevant essential health and safety requirements shall be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption", "hardware component transmitting signal or data, if relevant for connection or access to software that is critical for compliance, shall be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption"]
The Regulation adds essential requirement 1.1.9 of Annex III on protection against corruption. Software and data critical for compliance with the essential health and safety requirements must be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption. So must any hardware component that transmits signals or data, where it is relevant for connection or access to that software.
Evidence of A:
- software and data critical for compliance (1.1.9): requiresMeasure = adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption (condition: critical for compliance with the relevant essential health and safety requirements) | sentence: "Software and data that are critical for the compliance of the machinery or related product with the relevant essential health and safety requirements shall be identified as such and shall be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- hardware component transmitting signal or data (1.1.9): requiresMeasure = adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption (condition: relevant for connection or access to software that is critical for compliance) | sentence: "A hardware component transmitting signal or data, relevant for connection or access to software that is critical for the compliance of the machinery or related product with the relevant essential health and safety requirements shall be designed so that it is adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]

Answer B: ["connecting another device, directly or via a remote device, must not lead to a hazardous situation", "hardware components transmitting signals or data relevant to safety-critical software must be protected against accidental or intentional corruption", "the machine must collect evidence of legitimate or illegitimate intervention in that hardware", "safety-critical software and data must be identified and protected against accidental or intentional corruption", "the machine must identify the safety-relevant software installed on it and provide that information at all times in an easily accessible form", "the machine must collect evidence of legitimate or illegitimate intervention in, or modification of, its software or configuration"]
The Machinery Regulation, Annex III, section 1.1.9 'Protection against corruption', requires the following: connections must not create hazards, safety-critical hardware, software and data must be protected against corruption, the safety software installed must be identifiable, and interventions or modifications must be recorded. Art. 20(9) lets cybersecurity certification under Regulation (EU) 2019/881 give a presumption of conformity with this section. The passages do not include the Directive's full Annex I, so they confirm what 1.1.9 requires but do not themselves show that the Directive lacked it.
Evidence of B:
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "The machinery or related product shall be designed and constructed so that the connection to it of another device, via any feature of the connected device itself or via any remote device that communicates with the machinery or related product does not lead to a hazardous situation." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "A hardware component transmitting signal or data, relevant for connection or access to software that is critical for the compliance of the machinery or related product with the relevant essential health and safety requirements shall be designed so that it is adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "The machinery or related product shall collect evidence of a legitimate or illegitimate intervention in that hardware component, when relevant for connection or access to software that is critical for the compliance of the machinery or related product." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "Software and data that are critical for the compliance of the machinery or related product with the relevant essential health and safety requirements shall be identified as such and shall be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "The machinery or related product shall identify the software installed on it that is necessary for it to operate safely, and shall be able to provide that information at all times in an easily accessible form." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.1.9 | sentence: "The machinery or related product shall collect evidence of a legitimate or illegitimate intervention in the software or a modification of the software installed on the machinery or related product or its configuration." [REG, Annex III, 1.1.9]
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 20(9) | sentence: "Machinery and related products that have been certified or for which a statement of conformity has been issued under a cybersecurity certification scheme adopted in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/881 the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union shall be presumed to be in conformity with the essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex III, sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1, as regards protection against corruption and safety and reliability of control systems insofar as those requirements are covered by the cybersecurity certificate or sta" [REG, Art. 20(9)]

response.text: {"reasoning": "Both answers rest on the Regulation's Annex III 1.1.9 text, but neither evidence shows the Directive lacked it. A lists two items (software/data and hardware) and omits the connection-hazard, software identification and evidence-collection requirements that B also found. B's list is more complete and each item is stated by the evidence, though B notes the Directive's text is not shown. A's evidence does not show what is new relative to the Directive either, so it is no stronger on that point. B leaves out fewer items from 1.1.9.", "choice": "B"}
